title: Entero Healthcare Solutions Ltd - 544122 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Entero Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore and EBITDA margin reached 5.0%, already meeting full-year FY27 margin guidance.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% YoY to INR1,940 crore (40% like-for-like), with organic growth of 17.8% reported and 19.6% like-for-like versus an underlying pharma market growth of 13.8%. Gross margin expanded 147 bps to 11.4% and EBITDA margin expanded 143 bps to 5.0%, with EBITDA up 94% YoY. PAT rose 72% YoY to INR52 crore, but PAT attributable to owners was INR38 crore (up 37%) after INR14 crore of non-controlling interest. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~23% revenue growth ex-acquisitions, 5% EBITDA margin and 50% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, and said no major acquisitions are planned in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: entirely calendarisation of prior-year acquisitions; no new acquisitions in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR14 crore (~27% of PBT before minority interest)
financial_highlights.change: Q4 was about INR17 crore per the call

segments.name: Core pharma distribution
segments.commentary: Majority of business is demand fulfilment with lower gross margins; margin gains attributed to scale-driven procurement. Low-margin sub-distribution accounts exited, which reduced reported growth by about 2.5%.

segments.name: MedTech
segments.commentary: Organic MedTech revenue on track to exceed INR1,000 crore in FY27 and carries higher gross and EBITDA margins than core pharma. Management said the business plays a demand-generation role, not only fulfilment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: consolidated revenue growth of ~23% YoY excluding new acquisitions (about 11-12 points from calendarisation of prior acquisitions, rest organic).
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 5% maintained; management aspires to improve further and said H2 could beat guidance depending on H1 performance.
EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion of 50% on an annual basis; OCF is after working capital changes.
FY27 effective tax rate guidance of 22.5%; FY28 guidance to be given near FY27 close.
Interest cost expected to stay broadly in the same range as Q1 for the rest of the year.
Employee cost increments fell mainly in Q1 (effective 1 April); no major increase expected thereafter.

Medium-term: management said it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and modelling 20% is a safe assumption; ROCE of 25-30% was cited as possible in that period; internal aspiration EBITDA margin above 6%.
No revision to working capital days guidance; management will review after H1.
capex_capacity: Platform: 138 warehouses across 475 districts in 19 states; 72,000+ retail customers, 2,300+ hospital customers, 83,400+ SKUs, 3,000+ manufacturer relationships.
Depreciation: Q1 level expected to be the going-forward run-rate, subject to any major new capex; Q4 included depreciation on certain machines given to customers.
No major acquisitions planned for FY27, though a pipeline exists; a small Andhra Pradesh surgical consumables deal (with Sai Pharma) was completed and is immaterial to revenue.
Around INR200 crore of debt was taken for the last acquisition, disbursed late Jan/early Feb 2026.
demand_pricing: IPM growth has moved to double digits in the last two quarters (earlier 7-9%), driven mainly by volume; management could not isolate a specific cause.
Management said it cannot forecast future IPM growth and built its organic forecast on a lower industry growth assumption.
Growth above market is attributed to wallet share gains from better fill rates, product availability, range and more principal collaborations.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 FY26 through preponed government/diagnostic PPP billing, which made the sequential inorganic contribution look lower.
Management said MedTech has limited distributor competition and offers more scope for demand-generation contracts with higher gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the next 3-5 years without acquisitions, and what ROCE is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes it can grow at over 20% in the next 3-4 years, organically and inorganically, and sees ROCE of 25-30% possible at the end of that period.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the minority interest exist and when will the call options on it be exercised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said call options were agreed at deal signing at a valuation multiple matching the original acquisition, with exercise windows of 2-5 years; the minority is reinvested rather than paid out. Not all options fall due this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the sequential inorganic revenue contribution decline from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Q1 government project revenue was billed early in Q4 FY26 because of budget timing, so Q1 had a high base effect.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 one-off items recurring in other opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only part of the INR11.5 crore one-offs sat in other expenses; run-rate other expenses of about INR55 crore are expected to be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 5% EBITDA margin be a floor for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained 5% for the full year but said it targets quarter-on-quarter improvement and may revise guidance after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did minority interest fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minority share depends on subsidiary profit; Q4 had a revenue preponement at one subsidiary that boosted its profit share (INR17 crore in Q4 vs INR14 crore in Q1).

risks_watch: Growth in IPM has been unusually strong for two quarters and management cannot explain the cause, so sustainability is uncertain.
Non-controlling interest is about 27% of PBT and call-option buyouts (2-5 year horizon) will need funding, possibly from parent or subsidiary cash.
Q1 revenue was partly pulled into Q4 through government billing timing, so quarterly comparisons may be distorted.
Quarterly OCF is not disclosed; balance-sheet items (gross debt, net debt, OCF) will be given only at half-year and full-year, in September and March.
Interest cost is expected to stay at the Q1 run-rate after the INR200 crore debt drawdown.
Further exits of low-margin sub-distribution businesses could reduce reported growth again (about 2.5% impact in Q1).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and margins, and clear on the strategy to consolidate and grow organically. Management was evasive on IPM growth drivers, on the quantum of OCF and net debt, and on non-controlling interest funding.
key_quotes: We have started FY27 on a very strong footing. Consolidated revenue grew 38.2% year-on-year to INR1,940 crores.
We are pleased to have delivered our full year FY27 EBITDA margin guidance in the very first quarter of the year.
We always retain full operational and cash flow control over every one of these entities and minority share of profit is always reinvested in the business and not paid out.
When I say 50% of EBITDA getting converted to OCF, means EBITDA minus working capital changes, whatever is the remaining is supposed to be 50% of EBITDA.

We should not be looking at OCF on a quarter-to-quarter basis. We should be looking at an annual basis because -- and that's how I have given the guidance that on an annual basis, we will convert 50% of our EBITDA to OCF.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of ~23% revenue growth ex-acquisitions is held, with about 11-12 points from calendarisation of prior acquisitions and the rest organic, but the brief cites no new capacity, firm orders or contracts behind it; backing rests on demand/share gains, IPM growth in double digits, and MedTech scaling, which is an aspiration rather than specific numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 143 bps YoY to 5.0% in Q1 and gross margin rose 147 bps to 11.4%; management targets QoQ improvement and said H2 could beat the 5% FY27 guide, though run-rate other expenses of ~INR55 crore and the Q4 one-offs of INR11.5 crore weigh on the base.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or stores were discussed; the platform is 138 warehouses across 475 districts and the brief cites no capacity addition, so new capacity in the window is not signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Organic revenue grew 19.6% like-for-like vs 13.8% pharma market growth, IPM has moved to double digits for two quarters (earlier 7-9%), and FY27 guide of ~23% ex-acquisitions is held, with ~11-12 points from calendarisation and the rest organic; however, IPM driver is unexplained and growth is partly pulled from Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plan or utilisation figure was disclosed; depreciation at Q1 level is the going-forward run-rate subject to major new capex, and no major acquisitions are planned for FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.when: H2 FY27, after H1 results in September
rows.why: Management said H2 could beat the 5% EBITDA margin guide depending on H1 performance and may revise guidance after H1; the 23% revenue guide was only reiterated, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: All FY27 guidance (23% revenue growth, 5% EBITDA margin, 50% EBITDA-to-OCF) was reiterated with Q1 margin already at 5.0% and organic growth at 19.6% like-for-like; the main risk is IPM normalising, which is not a stated guide cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: MedTech is on track to exceed INR1,000 crore organic revenue in FY27 with higher margins and demand-generation contracts, but no specific new product or brand launch was named.

rows.label: Minority call-option buyouts need funding
rows.when: 2-5 year exercise windows; not all fall due this year
rows.why: Non-controlling interest is ~27% of PBT (INR14 crore in Q1) and options exercise over 2-5 years; ~INR200 crore of debt was drawn for the last acquisition, and funding source is unclear.

rows.label: Net working capital days down to 61
rows.why: NWC days fell to 61 from 66 a year ago, but management made no revision to working capital guidance and OCF is only disclosed at half-year and full-year.

rows.label: Medium-term 20%+ growth and ROCE 25-30%
rows.why: Management said it can grow over 20% organically and inorganically and ROCE of 25-30% is possible, with ROCE at 21.1% in Q1 (from 11.5%) and internal EBITDA aspiration above 6%; this is an aspiration, not guidance.
